title: Generative Molecular Morphing for Flexible-Size Design via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
claim: Morphing a random graph into a valid structure is a three-step procedure: match, interpolate with edits, then assign targets.
layout: 3 numbered panels, left-to-right, timeline of edit events in middle panel
description: A three-stage horizontal diagram with numbered circles: (1) Matching, (2) Interpolation, (3) Target assignment. Panel 1 shows a small source graph and a target graph beside a square assignment matrix. Its cells are colored blue for substitutions, red for deletions and green for insertions, with black epsilon rows and columns. Panel 2 is the largest. It plots node count N against time from 0 to 1, with the start graph g0 on the left and the end graph g1 on the right. A step-shaped line carries event markers: a red pentagon for del, blue stars for sub and a green triangle for ins. Small molecule graphs show nodes being deleted, moved and inserted. A gray box marks the intermediate graph g_t at time t. Panel 3 shows g_t with colored arrows toward g1, labeled sub, ins + movement + charge. Colors encode the operation type throughout.
caption: Interpolation between a randomly sampled graph ($t=0$) and a valid molecule ($t=1$). In the first step, we use the UOT matching to obtain edit sets determining whether nodes must be substituted, inserted or deleted. Given these sets, we interpolate to an intermediate graph $g_t$. Lastly, we assign the conditional generator matching targets.
abstract: The success of generative molecular design depends on a model's steerability toward high-reward samples. Because many molecular properties are intrinsically linked to molecular size, accurately capturing the joint distribution of properties and the number of atoms is essential. However, current diffusion and flow-based models fix the number of atoms, which ultimately limits their ability to navigate this complex relationship. To address this, we introduce Morph, a flexible-size generative model for conditional and unconditional 3D molecular design based on geometric graphs. By dynamically adapting size, Morph can seamlessly integrate existing structural priors, like scaffolds, and significantly enhances property steering. We show that Morph matches current fixed-size state-of-the-art models while significantly increasing sampling flexibility. We demonstrate out-of-distribution generation in regimes where previous models fail, paving the way for enhanced generative modeling for molecular design.
